tables.about: Every connection moves 1 MiB chunks, two commands in flight, each checked to the byte. CPU is every process of the binary (the proxy, and the relay), per GB moved.

Whole connections back to back, 8 at a time: dial, a one-byte echo, close. Connect-to-first-byte includes the proxy's SOCKS5 round trip to the data centre. Fronted is hellos the anti-replay cache took for replays (by the client; the cover listener's own count beside it).

One connection, 100 bytes to the data centre and 100 back, over and over. Direct is the same with no proxy and no SOCKS5: a door's added latency is its figure minus that one. Samples is how many round trips the percentiles rest on.

Connections opened and left open on a fresh process, each first proven with a one-byte echo. RSS is every process of the binary; per connection is the growth over the process before it, divided by the count. WEB is one session per connection.

metrics.title: mtgbench's own heap KiB per conn

tables.about: dd, 64 downloads: one user's 64 connections against 64 users of one each.
dd, 64 downloads: no cap, against a cap of 10 GB/s that never binds. The difference is the limiter's own cost.

64 ee connections on a fresh process whose clients read 100 KiB/s while the data centre sends as fast as it can, for 20 s, once. RSS per connection should stay near the doppelganger's bound (about 512 KiB of queue) and not grow with time.

tables.about: One user, 8 connections, against a cap of 1 or 10 MiB/s. speed-up is measured uploading, speed and speed-down downloading. Delivered bytes are sampled every second; the first (burst) second is dropped, and on ee the second after it too, which the doppelganger's queue (after the limiter) carries part of the burst into. Achieved over target: the mean, and the lowest and highest single second. Fairness is Jain's index across the user's connections (1 is equal shares).

Clean: one connection uploads 8 MiB and downloads 16 MiB; the proxy's /stats bytes_in and bytes_out, and for WEB the relay's bytes.up and bytes.down (less the client's 64-byte obfuscated2 frame), minus what the client moved. Every difference must be 0. Abrupt: the client asks for 64 MiB, reads 4 MiB and resets; the proxy may have counted bytes still in buffers, so counted ≥ received and counted ≤ what the data centre sent is the bound, and the gap is reported.
